units.label: line 7
units.text: 1. Summary

units.label: line 9
units.text: Meridian is a mobile scheduling and dispatch app for small HVAC and plumbing contractors with 3 to 25 technicians. It replaces whiteboards and phone calls with optimized daily routes, automated customer reminders and same-day job updates.

units.label: line 11
units.text: 2. Goals

units.label: line 13
units.text: Public launch on 15 March 2027, ahead of the spring maintenance season.

units.label: line 14
units.text: Reach 2,500 paying accounts within 12 months of launch.

units.label: line 15
units.text: Achieve $2.37M in annual recurring revenue by month 12 at an average of $79 per account per month.

units.label: line 17
units.text: 3. Growth plan

units.label: line 19
units.text: We assume paying accounts will grow 35% month-over-month from the 120 pilot accounts we already have, driven by contractor referrals and a partnership with regional supply distributors.

units.label: line 21
units.text: Pilot customers love the product, so conversion from pilot to paid should be close to 100%.

units.label: line 23
units.text: Customer acquisition cost is expected to stay below $180 per account because most growth will come from referrals.

units.label: line 25
units.text: 4. Scope

units.label: line 27
units.text: The MVP will be online-only. Offline support is deferred to v2 because technicians generally have reliable mobile coverage.

units.label: line 29
units.text: Route optimization will be provided by the PathCore Routing API. Customer SMS reminders will be sent through our existing messaging provider.

units.label: line 31
units.text: Support will be handled by the existing two-person customer success team.

units.label: line 33
units.text: 5. Budget

units.label: line 35
units.text: Total approved project budget: $1.2M, covering engineering, design, launch marketing and the first year of infrastructure.

units.label: line 37
units.text: 6. Risks

units.label: line 39
units.text: The main risk is competitor pricing. We will respond with a lower introductory price if needed.

units.text: Timeline

units.label: p.1 ¶5
units.text: Sprint 1 begins 5 October 2026. With two-week sprints, the release is planned as feature-complete at the end of sprint 12 on 21 March 2027.

units.label: p.1 ¶6
units.text: Feature-complete is followed by a 6-week hardening and beta period with selected pilot accounts.

units.label: p.1 ¶7
units.text: General availability is targeted for 2 May 2027.

units.label: p.1 ¶8
units.text: Team: 4 engineers and 1 product designer for the full plan.

units.label: p.2 ¶1
units.text: Requirements

units.label: p.2 ¶2
units.text: R-07 (P0): Offline job sync. Technicians must be able to view job details and record work while offline; changes sync when connectivity returns.

units.label: p.2 ¶3
units.text: Source for R-07: field interviews, where 14 of 20 technicians reported daily coverage gaps in basements and rural sites.

units.label: p.2 ¶4
units.text: R-11 (P0): Route optimization via the PathCore Routing API for up to 40 stops per technician per day.

units.label: p.2 ¶5
units.text: R-15 (P1): Customer SMS reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before each appointment.

units.label: p.3 ¶1
units.text: Dependencies and capacity

units.label: p.3 ¶2
units.text: PathCore Starter plan: 10,000 route requests per day, 99.5% monthly availability, no contractual SLA.

units.label: p.3 ¶3
units.text: Estimated load: each account averages 6 technicians and triggers about 4 route re-optimizations per technician per day.

units.label: p.3 ¶4
units.text: No fallback routing provider has been evaluated yet.

units.label: p.3 ¶5
units.text: Infrastructure costs are not included in this plan and are tracked by Finance.

findings.title: The 35% monthly growth assumption has no supporting evidence — pilot signups are flat
findings.summary: The business case rests on paying accounts compounding 35% month-over-month from 120 pilots. The pilot dataset shows roughly 20 new pilot accounts each month (after removing duplicate rows: 2026-03: 21, 2026-04: 19, 2026-05: 20, 2026-06: 22, 2026-07: 18, 2026-08: 20) — steady, not compounding. Reaching 2,500 accounts in 12 months from 120 requires 28.8% monthly compounding; no source shows that rate has ever been achieved.
findings.why_it_matters: Revenue, PathCore API load, support staffing and the budget envelope are all sized from this growth curve. If it is wrong, most downstream plans are mis-sized at the same time.
score_notes: 3 of 3 citations verified against extracted text.

findings.inference_note: The dataset records pilot signups, not paid conversions over time; it cannot prove what growth will be, only that nothing in it shows compounding.

findings.question: What evidence — referral rates, distributor pipeline, or a comparable launch — supports compounding growth rather than the flat ~20 accounts per month seen in the pilot?

nodes.label: The 35% monthly growth assumption has no supporting evidence — pilot signups are flat
nodes.detail: The business case rests on paying accounts compounding 35% month-over-month from 120 pilots. The pilot dataset shows roughly 20 new pilot accounts each month (after removing duplicate rows: 2026-03: 21, 2026-04: 19, 2026-05: 20, 2026-06: 22, 2026-07: 18, 2026-08: 20) — steady, not compounding. Reaching 2,500 accounts in 12 months from 120 requires 28.8% monthly compounding; no source shows that rate has ever been achieved.

nodes.label: A two-person customer success team cannot absorb onboarding at plan volume
nodes.detail: The brief keeps support with the existing two-person team. The onboarding workflow needs 90 minutes of customer success time per new account (30 minutes of setup plus a 60-minute call) within 48 hours. Even on a straight-line path to 2,500 accounts (~198 new accounts a month), onboarding alone needs about 298 hours a month, more than the 280 productive hours available — before any support tickets.
